text:
jen: Heads-up — we're rolling v0.9.3 to the canary pool in ~10m. Plan: deploy -> warm caches -> run a short sanity pass -> promote if green. @sam can you take primary watch?

alex: I can shadow. I'll run the quick verification script and watch latency + errors. ping me when deploy starts. :eyes:

maria: I'll pre-stage rollback artifacts and double-check db migrations are noop. rollback tag: v0.9.2-ready. :thumbsup:

sam: on call for watch. leaving a checklist here: 1) probe /health 2) run 5 sample prompts through the new model endpoint 3) check p95/p99, error rate, and token cost spike.

ops-oncall: I'll keep an eye on infra metrics (GPU queue size, autoscaler events, node OOMs). Alert thresholds: >5% 5m error rate OR p99 > 1s.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: canary-deploy-started at 1758491270 (image: registry.redwood/v0.9.3-canary).

alex: running verification now. curl health:
```
curl -sS https://canary.redwood.internal/health | jq .status
```

sam: results so far: health OK, small cpu bump on model-host-3 (~18%), requests succeeding 100/100 for first 30s.

maria: quick DB check confirms migrations not applied to canary group (expected). Rollback plan: scale down canary, route traffic back to v0.9.2, then demote images. I have infra runbook link: https://go/release-runbooks/v0.9 (shared).

alex: latency snapshot: p95=190ms, p99=420ms, error rate=0.12%. Token cost per request looks within expected band. No obvious quality regressions in the sample prompts.

jen: nice. if we stay stable for 10m and no alerts, promote to slice-1. Sam — you good to green-light?

sam: agree. green-lighting in 3m unless anything pops. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Deployment event: canary-promote-requested at 1758491295

ops-oncall: I'll keep slack watch for 30m post-promote. If any autoscaler thrash or error rate >0.5% escalate to paging.

jen: thanks everyone. tagging this thread 'light verification' for postmortem indexing. If any quick fixes are needed we'll open a tiny patch PR and coordinate here.
